analysis: Examined all supplied ProviderLoop.swift BASE source (lines 1–1178) and the complete changed-range patch. HEAD lines 787–796 add optional coordinator-connection diagnostics, unauthorized-duration/reconnect bookkeeping, and per-loop randomized recovery jitter. These declarations alone do not grant serving permission, change encryption, expose prompt/key material, or alter model/cache eligibility; no concrete regression is supported in this unit. Existing process-key generation, attestation signer initialization, slot memory limits, cancellation ownership, reconnect barriers, and artifact/cache identity separation provide surrounding context, not verification of their unchanged callers. Relevant contracts are A-016/TB-011 and T-052/T-053 (diagnostic versus serving authority and connection-bound grants), T-057 (recovery availability), and T-058 (accurate trust diagnostics). Integration must examine ProviderLoop+ServingAuthorizationRecovery and the new state's consumers: ensure unauthorized reconnects are bounded, respect active-work/drain barriers and connection generations, and cannot preserve or synthesize authorization; verify coordinatorConnection persistence accurately distinguishes transport state from permission. The supplied evidence does not include those behavioral changes or UnauthorizedConnectionRecovery's threshold policy, so their security conclusion remains unresolved. T-041's cache scoping, encryption, TTL, and donation controls are not changed by this patch.
